UPIC Pixel Blast adaptation — 2026-10-04

Official component:
https://github.com/DavidHDev/react-bits/blob/main/src/content/Backgrounds/PixelBlast/PixelBlast.jsx
Official showcase:
https://github.com/DavidHDev/react-bits/blob/main/src/demo/Backgrounds/PixelBlastDemo.jsx
Code-panel source:
https://github.com/DavidHDev/react-bits/blob/main/src/constants/code/Backgrounds/pixelBlastCode.js

The showcase imports the same component displayed in the code panel. Its
continuous movement comes from five-octave time-varying noise. Expanding rings
come from click events; pointer-liquid distortion is a separate optional effect.
The user's URL enables the default click ripples and leaves liquid disabled.

Reference parameters:
patternScale 0.25 / speed 1.35 / edgeFade 0.5 / density 1.65 / pixelSize 2.
License: see REACT-BITS-LICENSE.md in this directory.

UPIC retains noise/Bayer construction and ripple math with a shared market clock.
All numerical appearance controls are derived from chart data and measured sound
in pixel-blast-parameters.js, shared by both renderers. It is an adaptation, not
an identical standalone demo. The reference square is 2 CSS pixels; its rendered
requested width varies between 0.2 and 3.8 CSS pixels; rasterization rounds it
to whole device pixels with a minimum of one and keeps a black gap between cells. A fixed 4 CSS-pixel lattice reserves
room for this growth without moving pixel centres or zooming the scene.
The underlying noise-cell spacing stays fixed at 16 CSS pixels, independent of
the dynamic occupied square width.
Physical cell boundaries and dot bounds are integer-aligned in both renderers.
Rendering is bounded to 1.2 million pixels; very large surfaces can use a lower
pixel ratio. Canvas visits cells rather than every image pixel.

Mappings:
- pixelSize / dotSize: market cap, fresh activity and volume, measured level,
  formation, notes and transients determine the square width (0.2 to 3.8).
  The cellSize remains 4. The two size names are aliases for the same control.
- patternScale / scale: cap, liquidity, contextual movement and note accents
  vary the noise scale from 0.18 to 0.34 around the reference 0.25. This changes
  the texture inside the fixed viewport; camera and grid stay put.
- patternDensity / density: liquidity sets coverage around 1.65, with fresh
  flow and note/onset accents; the result is bounded to 0.65 through 2.6.
  Missing liquidity stays neutral; a known zero produces sparse coverage.
- speed: contextual movement, activity, volume, measured level, notes, onsets
  and the actual music tempo scale the shared clock around the 1.35 reference.
- edgeFade: liquidity, movement, sound, notes and pressure vary a narrow edge
  taper from 0.015 to 0.09, replacing the standalone reference's 0.5 spotlight.
  Only squares near the perimeter shrink, retaining binary coverage and sharp
  square edges while allowing the field to cover the full viewport.
- pixelSizeJitter / jitter: movement, flow and note/onset energy vary square
  sizes by 0 through 0.24. Pixel centres remain fixed.
- enableRipples / ripples: fresh significant movement, volume surges, notes or
  transients enable rings. Actual event keys seed their positions. Ripple speed
  (0.12 to 0.57), thickness (0.02 to 0.075) and rippleIntensityScale /
  rippleIntensity (0 to 1.75) follow movement, tempo, flow, sound and event energy.
- liquid / liquidStrength: movement, flow, sound, notes and onsets set distortion
  from 0 to 0.08. The radius (0.15 to 1.5) follows liquidity, cap, flow and sound;
  liquidWobbleSpeed (1 to 8) follows tempo, movement and note/onset energy.
  Distortion changes sampled field content on the fixed square grid. It does
  not displace raster cells or soften the rendered image.
- noiseAmount: fresh flow, movement and audio energy set 0 through 0.2 of
  deterministic field grain, evaluated on the same square grid.
- balance (0 to 1) retains observed buy/sell balance. Direction (-1 to 1)
  combines that balance and signed contextual price change, then applies
  freshness. A 5 percent move gives half the signed-change response; extreme
  changes approach the limit smoothly. Missing direction inputs stay neutral.
- ecosystem: liquidity and fresh flow/contextual movement set 0.18 through 0.36
  of regional density variation. A second deterministic noise layer forms
  distributed pockets across the viewport, with no centre mask or focal image.
  The former identity and identityMotion values remain as compatibility fields
  fixed at zero; market cap affects square size and texture instead of forming
  the coin artwork in the middle.
- Measured loudness and formation also set individual square brightness.

Liquid is adapted to affect field samples before rasterization,
instead of applying upstream's pointer-driven postprocessing distortion. Actual
market/audio events supply local direction. Nonzero direction vectors are
normalized; neutral audio touches use a fixed horizontal direction. Actual
measured envelope rises also create finite touches. The unwarped noise sample
cell is selected before continuous displacement, so sub-cell liquid motion
remains effective without moving or distorting the squares. Their influence has a Gaussian
radius of 0.12 times liquidRadius in height-normalized coordinates, follows the
source wobble expression, decays as exp(-age * 1.8), and ends after three seconds.
Noise is likewise sampled as field grain before sharp square rasterization.

The source control names and renderer aliases are exported together for the
inspector. No random parameter changes or invented trades/audio drive this map.
Market motion requires fresh observations. Measured sound and actual notes or
onsets can energize the effects even without a new market observation.
Quiet playback retains smaller, weaker squares and settles movement to rest.
Pausing disables ripples, liquid distortion, noise, jitter and the shared clock;
existing loudness/formation envelopes can settle in place. Reduced motion also
suppresses these effects and note/onset accents.

Deliberate fixed settings: variant is square to preserve the requested square
pixels; color is white; transparent is true for the existing background;
antialias is false for sharp binary raster edges; autoPauseOffscreen is true to
stop work when the visualization is hidden. These are structural and accessibility
choices rather than extra market signals. Alternate source shapes and colour
variation are intentionally excluded. The caller provides offscreen pausing.

Replay uses one relative presentation clock for noise and ripple age. Pausing
preserves phase, explicit seeks reset it, and candle-speed playback passes the
actual chart rate. Liquid wobble integrates its own phase from that clock and
its changing frequency, avoiding jumps caused by multiplying a large time by a
new frequency. Reduced-motion preference freezes flow and suppresses pulses.

Read source and reviewed changes statically. No browser or device audition was
performed for this revision.
